templates.v1:
A faithful, authentic rendering of the traditional Indonesian ornament: {subject}.
Style: monochrome line ornament only, pure solid black (#000000) strokes on a fully transparent background, no shading, no gradients, no grey, no texture, no text, no border, no frame.
Composition: a corner ornament like a letterhead flourish or document watermark — the motif is anchored in the bottom-right corner and grows from there, filling roughly the bottom-right two thirds and fading out (fewer, sparser elements) toward the top-left, which stays empty.
Accuracy matters more than decoration: keep the motif's real, recognisable shapes, proportions and symmetry as craftspeople make it; do not invent a generic spiral or mix in other cultures' motifs.
templates.v2:
A faithful, authentic rendering of the traditional Indonesian ornament: {subject}.
Style: single-colour line ornament, pure solid black (#000000) on a fully transparent background; no shading, no gradients, no grey, no texture, no text, no border, no frame.
Line weight (important, must be consistent): every stroke a uniform MEDIUM weight, about 10 to 14 pixels wide on this 1024 px canvas — no hairlines and no very thin double lines, and no large solid black filled areas or heavy silhouettes. Overall the black ink should cover roughly 15 percent of the canvas.
Composition: a corner ornament like a letterhead flourish or document watermark — anchored in the bottom-right corner, touching the bottom and right edges, filling roughly the bottom-right two thirds and thinning out organically (fewer, sparser elements, natural motif shapes) toward the top-left, which stays empty. Never cut the pattern off along a straight diagonal line.
Accuracy matters more than decoration: keep the motif's real, recognisable shapes, proportions and symmetry as craftspeople make them; do not invent generic spirals or mix in other cultures' motifs.

pintu-aceh.subject: Pinto Aceh (Pintu Aceh) from Aceh, Sumatra, as on the Pinto Aceh gold filigree brooch: a symmetrical gateway outline with a gently curved, pointed roof-like top and stepped shoulders, built of two or three concentric frames; the fields between frames filled with small filigree spirals and round dots like gold granulation, plus small Acehnese floral (bungong) sprigs. NOT Gothic tracery, NOT Thai temple ornament.

gorga.subject: Gorga, the carved ornament of the Batak Toba people (North Sumatra) on the gable boards of rumah bolon houses: ribbon-like strokes forming pairs of interlocking spirals that face each other (like curled fern shoots meeting), with a zigzag sawtooth border band (gorga ipon-ipon) of small triangular teeth along the bottom and right edges, drawn as outlines rather than filled shapes. NOT European/Celtic scrollwork, NO acanthus leaves.

pucuk-rebung.subject: Pucuk Rebung (Pucuak Rabuang), the Malay and Minangkabau bamboo-shoot motif from songket borders and Rumah Gadang wood carvings: tall, slender isosceles triangles like young bamboo shoots standing in a row along the bottom edge and climbing the right edge, each outlined and filled with a few nested chevrons and small curling tendrils, with small rebung shoots and curling sulur tendrils between them; the shoots get smaller and sparser toward the top-left so the ornament fades out organically — no straight diagonal cut-off edge.

megamendung.subject: Batik Megamendung from Cirebon, West Java: stacked rain-cloud forms with the characteristic pointed, triangular cloud tips and gentle inner curls, each cloud outlined by 3 to 4 concentric parallel outlines spaced well apart (not many thin hairlines)

kawung.subject: Batik Kawung from Yogyakarta, Java: four ellipses (stylised sugar-palm fruit) meeting at a centre point to form a four-petal cross, repeated on a square diagonal grid, with a small dot or cross in each gap

batang-garing.subject: Batang Garing, the tree-of-life motif of the Dayak Ngaju people of Central Kalimantan: a vertical spear-tip-shaped tree pointing upward, with paired branches curving symmetrically on both sides ending in curled tips, standing on a base with curled roots and a sacred jar (guci), surrounded by Dayak curling scroll ornament

patra-punggel.subject: Patra Punggel, the Balinese stone-carving ornament from candi bentar and kori agung temple gates, carved in soft paras sandstone: thick, plump, rounded lobes with deep grooves — each motif a fat mango-seed-shaped bulb (batun poh) from which a rolled curl (kuping guling) springs, edged with rounded scalloped lobes (ampas nangka) and a serrated crest (janggar siap), in the heavy, rounded, sculptural style of Balinese temple reliefs; units repeated along a diagonal running band. Chunky, rounded, Balinese. NOT European acanthus leaves, NOT baroque, NOT rococo, NOT Thai kranok flames.

pa-barre-allo.subject: Passura', the carved and painted wall ornament of the Toraja tongkonan house (South Sulawesi), as an elegant corner ornament: a few framed panels clustered in the bottom-right corner — one square panel with Pa' Barre Allo (a sun: a circle with short triangular rays), one with Pa' Tedong (a stylised, flat, geometric buffalo head with wide curved horns, carved-ornament style), a few Pa' Daun Bolu betel leaves and Pa' Bua Kapa' cotton-boll circles — the panels step down in size toward the top-left and toward the left, ending in small single motifs, never a long strip running to the left edge. Thin panel frames, open outlines. Geometric, angular. NOT baroque scrolls, NOT acanthus, NOT European flourish, NOT Greek meander, NOT Aztec, NOT a realistic cow face.

mamuli.subject: The Mamuli motif from Sumba, East Nusa Tenggara: the omega (Ω)-shaped mamuli gold ear ornament — a closed loop opening into two outward-curling feet with small decorative knobs — shown as a few large outlined mamuli forms arranged in a loose cluster with small Sumbanese ikat accents (stepped diamonds, small hooks) between them, as on hinggi cloth. Outlined, not filled.

tenun-tanimbar.subject: Tenun ikat Tanimbar (tais) from the Tanimbar Islands, Maluku: a few large, clearly readable warp-ikat motifs with the characteristic stepped, slightly feathered ikat edges — a stylised orchid (anggrek) flower as the main motif, with crescent moons, small paired flag shapes and twin arrowheads (tunis) as accents — arranged loosely, drawn as bold outlines. NOT cross-stitch, NOT embroidery, NOT Nordic knitting, NOT fleur-de-lis.

ukiran-asmat.subject: Asmat wood carving from southern Papua as on Asmat shields (jamasj), bis poles and canoe prows: a carved relief panel rising along the right edge and a carved band along the bottom, made of the characteristic Asmat forms — the praying mantis (wenet) as angular, bent, hooked limbs; hornbill heads with long curved beaks; the bipane (double-curved shell nose ornament) as mirrored back-to-back C-curves; flying-fox wing shapes — drawn as outlined relief shapes with open interiors and carved grooves, filling the corner evenly. NOT Maori koru, NOT tribal tattoo, NOT Celtic, NOT Pacific Northwest totem.
